title: How to Fix a Sold-Out Required Modifier on Delivery Apps
summary: When a shared menu option sells out, see which dishes can stay live, pause dishes you can’t serve as listed, and verify what customers see.
body_markdown:
When a shared delivery-menu option sells out, keep a dish live only if the remaining choices still satisfy its existing rules and the kitchen can make it as listed.


Mark the missing option unavailable in the system that controls the menu. Pause the dishes that fail either check and verify what customers see.


## One sauce sells out. Which dishes stay live?


Imagine the kitchen runs out of chipotle sauce. Three dishes use it, but they do not all need it in the same way:


- Grain bowl, choose one of two sauces:


Keep it live if the second sauce is in stock and selectable.
- Combo, choose two different sauces:


If only one in-stock option remains, pause the combo. Don’t lower its existing minimum just to keep it orderable.
- Signature chipotle wrap:


Pause it if the kitchen can’t make the wrap as listed. Don’t quietly make it with another sauce.


## Change the menu where it is controlled


Trace the ingredient across dishes, locations and apps. Two options with the same label may be separate records, not one shared choice. Use the point-of-sale (POS) system or integration if it owns the menu setting, or the merchant tool when it controls that listing. Avoid conflicting edits in both places.


[DoorDash’s Business Manager guide](https://merchants.doordash.com/en-us/learning-center/business-manager-app) describes updates to linked shared modifiers.[Uber Eats’ item guidance](https://help.uber.com/en/merchants-and-restaurants/article/c%C3%B3mo-actualizar-un-art%C3%ADculo?nodeId=862c8f0d-c0c1-48a6-b1b9-d2db8050bab8) describes repeating an update for separately listed occurrences. Controls differ by platform, integration and record type. Verify which setting applies to the option and the affected dishes.


## Check accepted orders and any automatic expiry


Check orders that already include the missing choice, including scheduled orders accepted for later. If you can’t serve one as placed, use the marketplace’s process to adjust it or cancel it if needed. If the stock setting expires automatically, assign someone to check supply before expiry and keep the affected items unavailable through a supported control if the shortage continues.


## Verify the storefront and restore in order


Without submitting an order, check each affected customer listing: the sold-out option should be unavailable, every dish you kept live should still offer a valid selection, and every dish you paused should not be orderable. This confirms the visible options, not kitchen fulfillment.


At restock, have the responsible person confirm the ingredient is physically available. Restore the option in the system that controls the listing before reopening dishes that depend on it. Recheck the customer view after the update.


Do you have to pause every dish that uses a sold-out option?


No. Keep a dish live when customers can still meet its existing selection rules and the kitchen can serve it as listed. Pause the dishes that cannot meet both conditions.


Use[Voosh’s delivery app listing audit](https://www.voosh.ai/blogs/delivery-app-listing-audit) for a broader storefront review. For online and offline visibility at the store level, explore[Voosh Marketplace Store Uptime](https://www.voosh.ai/marketplace-store-uptime) . Store-level status does not verify individual modifier choices.
